A VPN is a private tunnel between your device and another computer on the internet, which then goes online for you.

Normally, websites and your internet provider can see where your traffic comes from. With a VPN, everything you send is scrambled before it leaves your device, so your provider or the café Wi-Fi only sees unreadable data going to the VPN. The VPN then passes your request on, and websites see the VPN's address instead of yours.

It's good for safer public Wi-Fi and for hiding your location. It won't make you anonymous, though, since the VPN company can still see your traffic, so pick one you trust.
